audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Crushing Blow "shreds your armor (which is your whole defense)" and stops there. It never notices what that does to Ground Slam.
audit.why: Ground Slam deals magic damage BASED ON MALPHITE'S ARMOR. Crushing Blow's armour reduction is therefore not just a defensive debuff — it directly cuts the damage of your only trading ability, at the exact moment you want to use it. That is the decisive interaction of the whole matchup and it is absent from every field. It also reverses the trade order the page implies: you want Ground Slam out BEFORE he lands Crushing Blow, not as a response to it.
audit.corrected: Stated in early, mid, spikes[0], whys[0] and whys[2], with the sequencing rule (E first, then eat the shred) made explicit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E "deals magic damage based on his Armor")
champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Q "reduces the target's armor for a few seconds")

audit.whatIsWrong: "Watch for his W clone before you commit R" and "engage when his ult is down" are the two central instructions and neither carries a number.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is 22 seconds at rank 1 and still 18 at rank 5 — by a wide margin the longest cooldown in Wukong's kit and the single thing that can make your ultimate whiff. Cyclone is 130/110/90. Put together, the advice becomes countable instead of vague: after he burns the clone you have roughly twenty seconds where Unstoppable Force cannot be jukd, and from rank 2 onward his ultimate actually returns sooner than yours (110 to your 115, 90 to your 100), so you cannot bank on trading ults evenly.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster's 22-18s and the Cyclone-vs-Unstoppable-Force cooldown comparison added to spikes[1], spikes[3], mid, whys[4] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike and Stone Skin are never named or described; his engage is called "his E dash" once and his passive not at all.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike is a TARGETED dash onto you at 650 range on a 10-to-7 second cooldown — it is how every trade in this lane starts, and unlike a skillshot there is nothing to dodge, so the counterplay is spacing and the cooldown, not reaction. Stone Skin stacks armour and max-health regeneration while he fights, which is why extended trades drift to him even when the burst maths look even, and why Ground Slam's magic damage stays relevant against him while your autos do not.
audit.corrected: Both named with mechanics in early, mid, wants.foe[0] and whys[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (E "dashes to a targeted enemy", 650 range, 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7; P "stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting")

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart reads Wukong / Skill / Malphite / Malphite / Wukong / Malphite / Malphite, which disagrees with the prose in three places.
audit.why: whys[1] says "He still owns the trade" under a Skill label; whys[2] says "Most of his lethal trades happen here" under a Malphite label; and whys[4] plus spikes[1] both call Level 6 "your spike" and "your hardest all-in" under a Wukong label. early agrees with the prose: "Levels 1-3 are his". The chart is the outlier in every case.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 and 3 to Wukong, Level 6 to Malphite — Wukong / Wukong / Wukong / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite, which matches early, both spikes and the 51.78% win rate over 562 games.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are his — you have no trade pattern yet and he does. His Q shreds your armor (which is your whole defense) and his empowered autos out-DPS you while you just eat it, so do not contest the wave. Last-hit at range, take the chip, and let Granite Shield refresh between his trades. Do not flash-step into his auto range to throw a Q poke; you lose that exchange every time before W and E exist.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are his, and the reason is sharper than "he out-trades you": Ground Slam's damage is calculated from your armor, and Crushing Blow strips exactly that. Every trade he starts makes your one answer weaker. He opens with Nimbus Strike, a targeted 650-range dash you cannot dodge, so spacing is the only counterplay. Last-hit at range, take the chip, and let Granite Shield recharge between his trades rather than contesting the wave.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stabilize you as W (bonus armor, empowered AoE autos) and E (the attack-speed slow) come online — now his auto-reliant kit gets blunted and you can farm through his pressure even if it is still his lane on paper. Level 6 is your turn: Unstoppable Force gives you the pick threat he can't match. Watch for his W clone before you commit R — he'll drop a decoy to bait the knock-up, so R the real Wukong, then E to gut his attack speed and W to trade back. His R spin can knock you up mid-combo and reset, so engage when his ult is down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stabilize you: Thunderclap's bonus armor now outpaces Crushing Blow's shred, so Ground Slam keeps its damage and its attack-speed slow blunts an auto-reliant kit. Get E out before he lands Q, not after. Level 6 is your turn, and it is a counting exercise — Warrior Trickster is 22 seconds at rank 1, so R him inside that window and there is no decoy to eat the knock-up. Cyclone is 130s and can reset the fight, so engage while it is down. Stone Skin regenerates him through anything you drag out.

edits.before: This evens out and tilts your way as a frontline. From first armor item onward his Q-shred and AD autos struggle against a stacked-armor Malphite — your E permanently caps the attack speed his whole damage profile leans on. He stays item-dependent and can still W-clone juke your R in skirmishes, so the lane reads even because his outplay potential never fully dies, but in a straight teamfight your R engage and armor durability matter more than his single-target dive. Don't overchase a clone; pick your R for the carry, not for him.
edits.after: This tilts your way as a frontline. Once your armor stack is bigger than Crushing Blow's shred, Ground Slam holds its damage and permanently caps the attack speed his whole profile leans on. He stays item-dependent and can still juke your R with Warrior Trickster, so his outplay never fully dies — and from rank 2 his Cyclone returns before your R does, 110 to 115 and 90 to 100. In a teamfight your engage and durability beat his single-target dive. Pick your R for the carry, not for him, and never for a clone.

notes: One thing I checked and deliberately left alone: the entry never claims Wukong's clone can be revealed, and I did not add anything about it — Warrior Trickster grants Invisible, but nothing in the kit says whether Ground Slam's area damage or Thunderclap's aftershocks reveal or break it, and needsResearch is empty, which means unknown rather than no. Also carried over from the Zac mirror and applied here: Malphite's R carries a "projectile" flag that is a tooltip-parsing artefact — it is a dash, so nothing downstream should claim it can be blocked as a projectile.
